title: 2008 AMC 12A Problem 20
statement: Triangle \(ABC\) has \(AC = 3,\) \(BC = 4,\) and \(AB = 5.\) Point \(D\) is on \(AB,\) and \(CD\) bisects the right angle. The inscribed circles of \(\triangle ADC\) and \(\triangle BCD\) have radii \(r_a\) and \(r_b,\) respectively. What is \(\frac{r_a}{r_b}?\)

solutions.text:
By the Angle Bisector Theorem, \(AD:DB = CA:CB = 3:4,\) so \(AD = \tfrac{15}{7}\) and \(BD = \tfrac{20}{7}.\) The areas of \(\triangle ADC\) and \(\triangle BCD\) share base \(CD,\) so they are in ratio \(3:4,\) namely \(\tfrac{18}{7}\) and \(\tfrac{24}{7}.\)

Splitting \(\triangle ABC\) along \(CD,\) which meets each leg at \(45^\circ,\) gives \[ \dfrac{3 \cdot CD}{2\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{4 \cdot CD}{2\sqrt{2}} = 6, \] so \(CD = \tfrac{12\sqrt{2}}{7}.\)

The two semiperimeters are \[ \begin{aligned} s_a &= \dfrac{6}{7}(3 + \sqrt{2}), \\ s_b &= \dfrac{6}{7}(4 + \sqrt{2}). \end{aligned} \] Using \(r = \frac{\text{area}}{s},\) \[ \begin{aligned} \dfrac{r_a}{r_b} &= \dfrac{[ADC]}{[BCD]} \cdot \dfrac{s_b}{s_a} \\ &= \dfrac{3}{4} \cdot \dfrac{4 + \sqrt{2}}{3 + \sqrt{2}}, \end{aligned} \]

Rationalizing, \(\dfrac{4 + \sqrt{2}}{3 + \sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{10 - \sqrt{2}}{7},\) so \[ \begin{aligned} \dfrac{r_a}{r_b} &= \dfrac{3}{4} \cdot \dfrac{10 - \sqrt{2}}{7} \\ &= \dfrac{3}{28}(10 - \sqrt{2}). \end{aligned} \]

Thus, E is the correct answer.
